item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 16, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your MJR Morning Brief.
Cumulus Media has launched another round of nationwide layoffs, just weeks after emerging from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. The cuts have affected more than 20 radio markets, along with Westwood One. Among those departing are Greg Zoobeck, ending 44 years at Oklahoma City's Rock 100.5 KATT, and veteran broadcasters Tammy Daye, Faith Rinker and Lucy Ann Lance. The reductions also affect programming, management, sales and production positions. Cumulus has not disclosed a total number of layoffs.
Turning to television,
NBC is celebrating 100 years of broadcasting. The network was established November 15th, 1926, as America's first permanent radio network and went on to document some of the country's biggest moments while creating television institutions including TODAY, The Tonight Show, Meet the Press and Saturday Night Live. NBC's century also includes landmark coverage of the Olympics, Super Bowl, Apollo 11 and major breaking news events. NBC enters its second century as broadcasting continues its shift toward streaming and new platforms.
In radio news,
Beasley Broadcast Group reported third-quarter revenue of $42.8 million, down 16 percent from a year ago, and a net loss of $12.1 million. Digital revenue also declined, although digital profit margins improved. The company continues cutting expenses, selling assets and reducing debt as it works to rebuild advertising revenue.
Turning to music,
Taylor Swift is returning to the CMA Awards stage for the first time in 13 years. The two-time Entertainer of the Year will perform at the 60th Annual CMA Awards, hosted by Lainey Wilson, Wednesday, November 18, live on ABC and Disney+.
In radio news,
More than 8,000 people attended Johnjay and Rich's ninth annual LovePup Family Fest in Mesa, Arizona, where 70 rescue dogs found new homes. The free event featured Gavin DeGraw and raised money for animal rescue programs. LovePup plans to expand into Austin and San Antonio next year.
And finally,
Audacy launched a new weekly podcast Friday featuring former NFL star and WFAN personality Tiki Barber and his wife, Traci Johnson. “Double Down on Cheer with Tiki and Traci” explores competitive cheerleading, youth sports and parenting. The first episode featured Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi. New episodes arrive Fridays on major podcast platforms.
For the latest media news, job openings, free tools and more, visit MediaJobsReport.com.
